author: Codex /root/expanded_source_audit
reviewed_invariants: One real allocator-owned userdata stores four modular RNG words; its alignment and byte extent are checked before payload views. There is no separately allocated hidden RNG owner.
The module random and randomseed closures share the same actual userdata capture. A later opener creates another payload and cannot reseed the old closure pair.
New_Generator pins its payload before capture/closure allocations. The activation retains its closure and generator during RNG operations; ordinary tracing releases the userdata.
Both 32-bit arithmetic and native word paths read and write the selected captured state while retaining the existing transitions, warmup, range rejection and budget charging.
The nil-generator fallback serves existing private component tests; production module exports receive their owned captured generator.

Five separate C/AUnit cases cover old-stream preservation, independent advancement, retained capture roots, real userdata identity and sustained allocator refusal followed by recovery and balanced release.
limitations: Review covers the module RNG changes authored by the named author, not other changes sharing Machine or Library_Openers.
Local dirty Windows observations are not final clean-revision or cross-platform acceptance.
